newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb blast in Chechnya, Russia helicopter fired at.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast in Chechnya, Russia helicopter fired at.

text.p: A bomb exploded in the Chechen capital Grozny and a Russian helicopter was fired at from the breakaway territory in two separate incidents, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday. There were no casualties.
Interfax said the bomb exploded in central Grozny late on Monday, minutes after a convoy carrying Deputy Prime Minister Movlady Udugov passed the point.
The blast slightly damaged a neighbouring building and Interfax quoted Interior Ministry officials as saying they did not rule out a possible assassination attempt against Udugov.
Earlier on Monday shots from automatic weapons were fired at a Russian military helicopter patrolling the border between Chechnya and the neighbouring region of North Ossetia.
The pilots were unharmed but several bullet holes scarred the helicopter, Interfax said.
Russia pulled its last troops out of Chechnya in January after almost two years of bloody war with local separatists.
Rebel guerrilla commander Aslan Maskhadov was elected president of the region in January and his government is now trying to map out a new relationship with Moscow.

Under last August's peace accord the two sides agreed to postpone a decision on Chechnya's final status for five years. But the separatists claim their republic is already independent, despite a lack of international recognition, while Moscow insists that it remains part of the Russian Federation.
